R0278.title: Embodied-Intelligence Data-Collection Privacy Leakage
R0278.definition: The risk that privacy data collected by robot-mounted cameras, microphones, and LiDAR in homes, malls, and factories is leaked, stolen by attackers, or abused by vendors.
R0278.description:
Embodied-intelligence data-collection privacy leakage is a core privacy risk as service robots proliferate. The iRobot Roomba J7 dev unit captured private home images (including a woman on the toilet, children) via a low-angle front camera; the data was sent to Scale AI's Remotasks platform for annotation, and annotators illicitly shared screenshots to private Facebook groups and Discord. Amazon Astro was called a "privacy nightmare" by internal engineers, equipped with a telescoping camera and face recognition. Ecovacs robots were broken by security researchers in 2024, allowing real-time camera viewing and photo/audio theft; multiple cities saw Deebot X2 units remotely hijacked to shout racial slurs via the speaker. The LidarPhone research showed a robot-vacuum LiDAR can be repurposed as a laser microphone, recovering conversations even on devices without a microphone.

This risk relates to R0211 (smart-home privacy eavesdropping) and R0078 (data leakage), but is specialized for the physical-world collection scenario of embodied-intelligence devices, a core issue for GDPR and Personal Information Protection Law compliance.
R0278.influence: Causes leakage of private home images, children's privacy, and trade secrets; usable for extortion, precision scams, or social engineering; vendor abuse of collected data for model training also raises informed-consent and data-sovereignty disputes.
